stories.headline: ESPN's AFL Misery Index: Which club would you have least wanted to support since 2000?
stories.summary: Which AFL club has had the most success since the turn of the century? Which teams' fans have had a miserable existence since 2000? We've ranked each club on our Misery Index.
stories.body:
Which AFL club would you have wanted to support most since the turn of the century? Of course, the answer to that question has to be your own team, but if we did get a second choice, who would you pick? In other words, which club has provided its fanbase with the most happiness? On the flip side, which team has provided the most disappointment?

Welcome to ESPN's AFL Misery Index.

This is a countdown of the teams that have given its fans with the least amount of joy since 2000. I'm not just looking at premierships and win percentages, but also finals records, droughts, off-field issues, as well as the ability to draft well and attract free agents.

Let's get into it, beginning with the team you would have most wanted to support!

18. Geelong
Record: 422-6-217 (65.9%)

Premierships: 4

Finals series/finals: 21/53

Bottom four finishes: 0

The Cats may not have won as many flags as the Lions in this period but what this club has going for it is sustained relevance and competitiveness since basically the turn of the century. Geelong just doesn't know how to be bad and if you're a fan born in 2000 you would have already witnessed your team win four premierships, play in seven Grand Finals, and feature in a staggering 15 preliminary finals. The Cats have also had more stability than anyone else, with just two coaches in the last 26 years. And to cap off the perfect supporter experience, Geelong is now just about the destination club for free agents and homesick Victorians.

17. Brisbane

Record: 331-6-297 (52.7%)

Premierships: 6

Finals series/finals: 14/41

Bottom four finishes: 8

Some will argue vehemently that it's insane to not have the Lions sitting top of this list given the club has won six premierships (and completed two separate three-peats) since 2000. Granted, that's more success than anyone else, and it's not particularly close. But between these two modern day dynasties, Brisbane was a complete rabble. In fact, the club featured in finals just once from 2005 to 2018 -- that's half of the period we're taking into consideration here! You'd love to have supported this mob, no doubt, but the Cats simply have to pip them for top spot based on their significantly higher floor.

16. Hawthorn
Record: 351-6-274 (56.1%)

Premierships: 4

Finals series/finals: 15/38

Bottom four finishes: 4

Of all the dynasties we've witnessed since the turn of the century, was Hawthorn's the best? There's a real argument to be made the dominance of this club, under Alastair Clarkson, tops anything else we've seen in recent times. The Hawks were the envy of the competition between 2008 and 2015, winning four flags with one of the greatest teams ever assembled. You'd be pretty thrilled going to the footy each week and watching both Lance Franklin and Cyril Rioli running around in your forward line! With Zach Merrett and Ben King being added to the mix this current offseason, Hawthorn is once again a premiership favourite.

15. Sydney
Record: 380-6-254 (59.8%)

Premierships: 2

Finals series/finals: 21/47

Bottom four finishes: 2

When you consider the Swans have played in seven of the last 21 Grand Finals and own the second-best win percentage since 2000, there's a strong argument they should rank higher on this list. But, of course, five of those Grand Finals ended in heartbreaking defeat. In the last two Grand Final losses, they've been belted off the park. That really stings! As does the recent Pullman Hotel saga involving a number of the club's most high-profile players. Still, there would be many footy fans selling their souls to the devil to have what the Swans have had this millennium.

14. Collingwood
Record: 361-8-267 (57.4%)

Premierships: 2

Finals series/finals: 17/43

Bottom four finishes: 4

The Magpies have provided their passionate fanbases with real bang for their supporter buck over the last 26 years. Of course, there's been six Grand Finals and two memorable triumphs, but also 17 finals series and 12 preliminary final appearances. Basically, just about one in every two years Collingwood is still alive at preliminary final weekend! The club has also avoided bottoming out and made a habit of immediately catapulting itself back up the ladder whenever they've suffered a down season. Say what you want about the Magpies army, but they've certainly experienced happiness since 2000.

13. Richmond
Record: 272-9-331 (45.2%)

Premierships: 3

Finals series/finals: 9/19

Bottom four finishes: 9

What an incredible four-year period it was for the Tigers between 2017 and 2020 where it played in three Grand Finals and won all three. Talk about capitalizing on your premiership window! From a fan perspective, the best part of the era might have been getting to watch three-time Norm Smith Medal winner and club legend Dustin Martin play each of his 302 games. However, outside of that dominant four-year block, Richmond managed to win just one final (in 2001) and finished in the bottom four on nine occasions, three times collecting the wooden spoon. Things also don't appear to be improving any time soon.

12. West Coast
Record: 291-4-327 (47.1%)

Premierships: 2

Finals series/finals: 14/29

Bottom four finishes: 9

Since 2000, the Eagles have played in four Grand Finals, winning two and losing two. Both flags were incredibly memorable. In 2006, West Coast got its revenge against Sydney, winning the thrilling decider by a solitary point. In 2018, they stormed over the top of Collingwood, a game that will forever be remembered for Dom Sheed's late brilliance in the pocket. Had it not been for an absolutely dire last five years -- arguably the worst 100-game stretch in the AFL era -- this club would probably have been in the top four. Still, Eagles fans continue to show up and support the club through its dark times.

11. Western Bulldogs
Record: 307-5-308 (49.9%)

Premierships: 1

Finals series/finals: 13/27

Bottom four finishes: 5

The Bulldogs are usually there or there abouts. A memorable breakthrough flag in 2016 provided so much joy to the loyal fanbase that had been starved of success for so long. They then returned to the Grand Final in 2021, losing to the Demons in the west. Before the Luke Beveridge era, the Bulldogs also enjoyed a strong patch under Rodney Eade, reaching three consecutive preliminary finals between 2008 and 2010. This club continues to employ Marcus Bontempelli, one of the greatest players of the generation, and just landed superstar midfielder Zak Butters. There's plenty to be chuffed about if you support the Dogs.

10. Port Adelaide
Record: 333-3-288 (53.6%)

Premierships: 1

Finals series/finals: 13/31

Bottom four finishes: 4

This club has played in two Grand Finals since the turn of the century. The first, in 2004, resulted in a premiership and denied Brisbane a fourth successive flag. The second, in 2007, resulted in the greatest loss in Grand Final history, a 119-point defeat at the hands of Geelong. Port Adelaide has not been back to the big dance since that day but under Ken Hinkley they were a picture of consistency for a decade, reaching four preliminary finals since 2014. Did you know that only Geelong, Sydney, Collingwood, and Hawthorn have won more games than the Power since 2000?

9. Adelaide
Record: 330-2-289 (53.3%)

Premierships: 0

Finals series/finals: 14/29

Bottom four finishes: 4

The Crows have been average to decent for much of the last 26 years, which has to rank them somewhere in the middle. How does ninth sound?! This club has the best winning percentage since 2000 of teams that haven't won a premiership in the period, and sixth-best overall. They have also claimed three minor premierships in that time and outside of the shortened 2020 season haven't ever really had a bad year. But despite all of that, Adelaide has only featured in one Grand Final (where it started as a significant favourite and lost). That 2017 heartbreak against Richmond was followed by an infamous pre-season camp and seven-year September drought.

8. Melbourne
Record: 266-4-343 (43.7%)

Premierships: 1

Finals series/finals: 10/20

Bottom four finishes: 8

The 2021 premiership is doing plenty of heavy lifting for the Demons here. In fact, without that flag there's a real argument Melbourne should be on the bottom of this list. From 2005 to 2017 this club experienced the lowest of lows, routinely belted off the park and never coming close to playing finals. Who can ever forget that humiliating 186-point loss to the Cats in 2011 -- the second-greatest defeat in league history? But all (well, most) was forgotten with that breakthrough flag at Optus Stadium, though that in itself was a sore point for many of the Demons faithful who missed out on witnessing it in the flesh! The fact this club still hasn't won a final since that day is wildly disappointing.

7. Fremantle
Record: 304-3-308 (49.7%)

Premierships: 0

Finals series/finals: 10/22

Bottom four finishes: 5

After this year's extraordinary Grand Final capitulation against Brisbane, maybe it wouldn't be outrageous for the Dockers to be at the bottom of this list. After all, has anything more demoralizing ever happened to a footy team on the field? I'm not so sure. It's now two Grand Finals Fremantle has played in and on both days they could probably consider themselves the better team. Yet the club still awaits its inaugural premiership. The fact the Dockers' list is in such a great spot right now, and is set up for the next half decade (at least) probably saves them from dropping a few more rungs here.

6. St Kilda
Record: 282-8-323 (46.7%)

Premierships: 0

Finals series/finals: 9/20

Bottom four finishes: 6

Saints fans will argue they must be lower on this list, but remember, we're only talking from 2000 onwards. Since the turn of the century, this club has featured in three Grand Finals. Sure, one of them was a replay, and they were unable to win any of them, but simply being in those positions is far more than can be said for any of those ranking below them. What's incredibly tough to swallow for St Kilda supporters is seeing the club fall agonisingly short when they were competitive, a period which has been sandwiched by prolonged middling stretches. In other words, irrelevance.

5. GWS
Record: 164-4-180 (47.7%)

Premierships: 0

Finals series/finals: 8/19

Bottom four finishes: 4

Remember when the media was convinced the Giants were going to win the next 10 premierships? Well, that aged like milk. GWS currently sits on zero flags, but the club did feature in the 2019 Grand Final, a day they were humiliated by Richmond. And then of course there was the home semifinal loss to eventual premier Brisbane in 2024, a game in which they led by 44 points. Oh, and the heartbreaking 2016 home preliminary final loss to the Bulldogs, another eventual premier. This club has had no shortage of talent but nothing to show for it. Its two best players, Jeremy Cameron and Toby Greene, have also both ultimately wanted to leave.

4. Essendon
Record: 276-7-328 (45.7%)

Premierships: 1

Finals series/finals: 11/18

Bottom four finishes: 8

Essendon's 2000 premiership might well have saved the club from last spot on this list, because since then they have basically lurched from one disaster to the next. There was heartbreak the following year with a Grand Final defeat to Brisbane, before three consecutive semifinal losses. The Bombers have now not won a final in 22 years, something that's become a meme in footy circles. Essendon also endured the biggest off-field saga this century with its involvement in the infamous supplements saga that led to coach sackings and player suspensions, setting the club back years. To cap it off, captain Zach Merrett begged to be traded, wasn't, and then was. Grim.

3. North Melbourne
Record: 256-5-349 (42.4%)

Premierships: 0

Finals series/finals: 9/17

Bottom four finishes: 10

No team has finished in the bottom four more times since 2000 than North Melbourne. Even the 'good' periods were hardly worth celebrating, back-to-back preliminary final losses in 2014 and 2015 were followed by an elimination final loss in 2016 and then a dreadful, competition-worst 10-year finals drought. The Kangaroos have had nine coaches (Jaymie Graham will be the 10th) in the last 26 years and in many ways have forgotten what it feels like to win. The fact Nick Blakey is seen as the club's saviour proves attracting free agents and marquee signings has been slim pickings for this mob.

2. Carlton
Record: 242-6-362 (40.2%)

Premierships: 0

Finals series/finals: 9/17

Bottom four finishes: 9

From the salary cap breach and draft pick punishment to a merry-go-round of coaches, there's been setback after setback for the Blues in the 21st century. This club has claimed a league-high five wooden spoons since 2000 (they had zero prior to 2000) and forced its fans to witness its most barren and disappointing stretch in history. The best moment in 26 years was a stirring semifinal win over Melbourne in 2023, which tells you all you need to know about how much this club has been starved of success in the modern era.

1. Gold Coast
Record: 114-2-237 (32.6%)

Premierships: 0

Finals series/finals: 1/2

Bottom four finishes: 9

Question: what's this club's greatest moment in history? Answer: a one-point win over Fremantle in an elimination final in 2025. Literally every other team has enjoyed a significantly higher peak this century, which has to place the Suns dead last on our ranking. That memorable final was one of just two finals Gold Coast has ever played and the only finals series it has qualified for (everyone else has at least eight in this time!). Season 2025 remains the only campaign in which the Suns won more games than they lost. Gold Coast also has easily the worst winning percentage of any club. Yeah, supporting this team has brought basically zero happiness.

stories.headline: WNBA Finals saw surge in attendance and record ratings
stories.summary: The WNBA Finals were the most watched since 1999, with an average of 1.88 million people viewing the seven-game series that Golden State won over Atlanta in a decisive
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- The WNBA Finals were the most watched since 1999, with an average of 1.88 million people viewing the series that Golden State won over Atlanta in a decisive Game 7.

That game averaged 3.3 million viewers, making it the most-watched WNBA postseason game ever. It was up 128% from last season's clinching game between Las Vegas and Phoenix that the Aces won.

All seven games in the series were sold out, including Game 6, which was played at 12:30 p.m. EDT.

The Finals capped the WNBA's most-watched postseason since its inaugural season in 1997, averaging 1.49 million viewers, up 27% from last year.

stories.headline: Ravens look to stabilize crumbling season with QB Jacoby Brissett
stories.summary: Given the veteran QB's recent track record, it remains to be seen whether Baltimore can truly salvage its season.
stories.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- The Baltimore Ravens have dropped three straight games, lost star quarterback Lamar Jackson indefinitely and watched their playoff hopes quickly crumble.

Still, Baltimore is not throwing in the towel at the midway point of a 2026 NFL season that's spiraling downward.

The Ravens are finalizing a trade for Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, which shows they're not giving up on the season. But, given Brissett's track record, the Ravens have a better chance of stabilizing the season than saving it.

Baltimore (4-4), which is in last place in the AFC North, has a 6.4% chance of making the playoffs and an 0.5% chance of winning the division, according to ESPN Analytics. With such dismal odds and the uncertainty surrounding Jackson, Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta could have considered punting on the final nine games of the season by trading some starters and acquiring more picks for what is supposed to be a loaded 2027 draft.

Instead, the Ravens are trying to salvage a season that has been devastated by injuries at quarterback. Jackson is expected to go on IR with a right thumb injury he suffered in Sunday's 36-10 loss at the Buffalo Bills and is potentially out for the rest of the season. To make matters worse, Tyler "Snoop" Huntley, Baltimore's top backup, is out for the season with turf toe, according to Schefter and Rapoport.

The trade is a move that can curb a free fall in Jesse Minter's first year as a head coach and Declan Doyle's first as an offensive playcaller. The veteran Brissett offers hope of fielding a competitive offense.

The Ravens are so desperate at quarterback that they're starting undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who practiced with a brace on his injured right ankle, for Thursday night's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Baltimore's other two active quarterbacks on Thursday are Kedon Slovis and Austin Reed, both of whom were signed within the past three days. This means that the Ravens' three quarterbacks -- Fagnano, Slovis and Reed -- have combined for no previous starts, 23 pass attempts and no touchdown throws.

Brissett, 33, provides much-needed experience at quarterback but not a winning track record. He's never had a winning record in any of his 11 NFL seasons, losing 16 of his past 19 starts.

His career record of 23-50 (.315) is the second worst in the NFL among quarterbacks with at least 50 starts over the past decade. The only quarterback with a worse record over that span is Justin Fields (16-37, .302).

The reason Brissett is available is that he was benched by the Cardinals (3-5) and dropped to No. 3 on the depth chart. Baltimore has familiarity with him because Ravens quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork was Brissett's quarterbacks coach in Arizona last season.

Brissett has thrown 86 career touchdowns, which gives Baltimore a chance to get the offense out of its rut. The Ravens have been held to 14 points or less in three straight games, which hadn't happened in Baltimore in 21 years.

Even though Baltimore has been without Jackson for a majority of the season, the Ravens still have playmakers on offense in running back Derrick Henry and wide receiver Zay Flowers. But over the past three weeks, Baltimore has been among the worst offenses in the league with off-target throws, poor offensive line play and penalties. Since Week 6, the Ravens have totaled more false starts (eight) than touchdowns (three).

It has been a startling turn of events for the Ravens, who entered the season as one of the Super Bowl favorites and started 4-1. Baltimore's season unraveled after that when Jackson hurt an ankle and hand.

With half the season left, there are several 30-or-older Ravens who aren't in a position to resign themselves to a lost season, from Henry to defensive end Calais Campbell to offensive tackle Ronnie Stanley. It'll just be a difficult challenge if Jackson doesn't return this season. Baltimore is 7-14 (.333) since 2019 when Jackson hasn't been its starting quarterback.

The addition of Brissett gives the Ravens a better option at quarterback than they had. But it remains to be seen whether Brissett improves their chances at turning the season around.

stories.headline: Athletics hire Brewers' Cam Castro as new general manager
stories.summary: The Athletics have hired the Brewers' Cam Castro to be their new GM. Castro served as Milwaukee's senior vice president of player development and performance.
stories.body:
LAS VEGAS -- Athletics president of baseball operations Taylor Smith made his first major decision since taking over two weeks ago, going to World Series champion Milwaukee to hire Cam Castro on Wednesday as general manager.

Castro, 36, was the Brewers' senior vice president of player development and performance. He was with the club for eight years, serving as the liaison between the front office and the coaching staff regarding player development.

"The A's are a historic franchise with an incredible legacy," Castro said in a statement. "I look forward to being a part of the next chapter of A's baseball and developing a team, culture and organization that our fans will be proud of."

The A's, who went 64-98 this season, are rebuilding their front office in anticipation of the organization's planned moved to Las Vegas in 2028. They are scheduled to play their third and final season next year at a Triple-A ballpark in West Sacramento, California.

Hiring Smith, who previously was with the Red Sox and Rays, began that makeover.

"Cam will be an awesome addition to the front office and a great partner to me in running this organization," Smith said in a statement. "He has experiences and skillsets that will complement me and the very talented people that we already have in the organization. He's one of the best development minds in the game with a proven track record of building the systems and processes that develop a winner."

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton: Watching successor Kimi Antonelli win title 'highlight of my year'
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton has said watching his Mercedes successor Kimi Antonelli win his first world championship was the "highlight" of his Formula 1 season.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton has said watching his Mercedes successor Kimi Antonelli win his first world championship was the "highlight" of his Formula 1 season.

Antonelli, who replaced the seven-time world champion at Mercedes at the start of 2025 following his move to Ferrari, clinched the title at Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix, becoming the youngest champion in F1 history at just 20 years old.

Hamilton, along with fellow multiple title-winner Max Verstappen, celebrated Antonelli's achievement on the podium and praised the Italian in a post on social media on Monday.

"Let me start with a huge congratulations to the new champion, Kimi Antonelli," Hamilton, 41, wrote on Instagram. "To have seen your journey so closely and to be there celebrating with you, was a highlight of my year. So well deserved and a record that will stand for a long time.

"It was great to see your team at Mercedes celebrating with you. Enjoy this moment, keep your family close, keep your passion and your energy."

Antonelli was just 18 when he stepped into Hamilton's seat at Mercedes, facing the daunting task of replacing the most successful driver in F1 history, who won six of his seven world titles with the Silver Arrows.

But the Italian has enjoyed a remarkable second season, beating teammate George Russell and Ferrari's Hamilton -- among others -- to the championship with four rounds still scheduled to take place.

Hamilton's congratulations came alongside an admission of frustration over Ferrari's weekend in Mexico, where he felt the team had missed an opportunity to win and also appeared to acknowledge tensions following Charles Leclerc's actions on the opening laps.

"Our own weekend was one full of challenges," Hamilton said. "We had a lot thrown at us but our mechanics and engineers did an incredible job.

"We've grown so much together this year, and that progress has taken a huge effort from everyone on the track and back at the factory. That's why losing what could've been a win hurts so much.

"We need to grasp every opportunity we have, so it's incredibly frustrating, and I can't pretend otherwise."

- Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari have 'big problems' after Charles Leclerc incident

- Hamilton demands 'serious talks' at Ferrari, questions Leclerc's 'mentality'

He added: "Battling is necessary, but when that battle costs the team, we have to be honest about it and learn from it.

"We can push each other to the limit and still honour the responsibility to everyone who put us on that track."

Despite his frustrations, Hamilton insisted his commitment to Ferrari remained unchanged.

"I'll keep giving everything I have. My belief in this team hasn't changed and neither has my responsibility to help us get this right," he said.

"Stick with us. I'm only just getting started with this team, and we have so much more to come."

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Miami finds its feet with Decision Day coming up
stories.summary: Which teams are in the best position heading into Decision Day? All this and more in the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday and another weekend of action is in the books. With Decision Day coming up next week, it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings to see which teams are in a good or bad spot to qualify for the MLS Cup playoffs.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

While seeking history on a rainy night in Tennessee, Nashville fell behind by two goals, had multiple goals called off, but battled back to force two own goals and clinch a 3-2 win against Red Bull New York with stoppage-time headed goal from Sam Surridge. The Supporters' Shield winners are level with Miami's points record, but could break it with just a point from their final game.

2. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 2

Miami reclaimed second place in the Eastern Conference with a second-half rally against the Revs to win 2-1, ignited by the guy still leading the Golden Boot race: Lionel Messi. After a headed assist to Germán Berterame to level the score, Messi scored his 26th goal of the year after finagling past multiple defenders then sending a low left-footed strike past Matt Turner.

3. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 4

The Revs' four-game win streak came to a halt against the Herons, as Messi proved the difference maker once more assisting and scoring in a come-from-behind win for Miami. With that, New England drops to third place in the Eastern Conference. Silver lining? Dániel Gazdag is now on a two-game scoring streak.

4. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 3

STL had the firepower in the attacking third to come away with all three points against San Diego. But thanks in part to Pablo Sisniega's six saves and Anders Dreyer's moment of quality, they went home with a 1-0 defeat instead. The playoffs were already locked up but home-field advantage isn't as they head into the final weekend.

5. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 5

After going scoreless in six games, Robert Lewandowski came off the bench to make the difference in Colorado, providing the go-ahead goal 10 minutes after subbing on, then setting up Puso Dithejane for the 4-2 win.

6. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 7

The Whitecaps showed their quality in a comprehensive 5-1 dismantling of Seattle, highlighted by a Brian White brace that started in the 56th minute. After a 4-1 win over San Diego in midweek and 29th-place Montréal up next, the Western Conference's first-place side have got some momentum ahead of the postseason.

7. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 6

After drawing Nashville 0-0 in the midweek, Philly's 1-0 loss to Cincinnati is their second in three games. They'll be in the postseason, but they may have a tough matchup when it comes.

8. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 9

With the Golden Boot technically still in reach, Petar Musa (who scored 22 goals this season) missed his first penalty in six this season in the 97th minute. Stefan Cleveland's late-game save kept the Toros from three points in a 1-1 draw as they head into the final weekend looking to secure second place in the Western Conference.

9. LAFC
Previous ranking: 8

After losing 3-1 to Minnesota, LAFC are winless in three (two draws) ahead of a Decision Day battle with the Sounders. With their playoff place secure, they're competing for a better finish in the standings, but will fall short of their top-three finish in the Western Conference in the last four seasons.

10. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 13

Kristijan Kahlina, whose save percentage (75.9%) is second only to first-place Nashville's Brian Schwake (77.7%), stopped eight against Orlando in a match that ended 4-0 in Charlotte's favor, despite both teams firing off the same number of shots (and nearly the same on target, though Charlotte had higher quality opportunities).

11. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 11

After losing 4-0 to mid-table side Charlotte, Orlando picked up their first defeat in six games but still clinched their playoff spot based on other results. They're in the final wild card spot ahead of a final test against the Revs.

12. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 15

The Quakes took 17 minutes to score twice against RSL, and that was enough to secure three points in a 2-1 win. That's their first win in six (four draws, one loss) as they look to secure their third-place spot in the Western Conference.

13. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 10

In a 5-1 loss to Vancouver, Jordan Morris' brief light of life in the second half was overshadowed by the Whitecaps' rapid response in a match characterized by goalkeeper Andy Thomas looking painfully skyward for help from the scoreline. After losing to Houston in midweek, the Sounders have three defeats and no wins from their last five games. They play LAFC on the final day while sitting one place short of the wild card spots.

14. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 14

Morgan Whittaker scored from close range to mark his third goal in three games and take an early 1-0 lead against Chicago. But at the end of a goal-heavy matchup, Lewandowski scored and assisted off the bench to help see the Fire to a 4-2 win. The Rapids ended the weekend in the final playoff position and have a tough final test against Dallas to hang on.

15. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 17

Cincinnati only forced one save out of Andre Blake, but with the help of Roman Celentano's six stops, they booked their playoff spot with a 1-0 win against the Union. Ayoub Jabbari came off the bench in the second half and registered the sole tally of the night, capitalizing on Blake's save (a low-struck ball from Evander) to score off the rebound.

16. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 16

The Dynamo could secure home advantage in the playoffs with a top-of-the-table finish, but are hanging on to fifth place ahead of the final day after losing 3-1 to Portland (their first loss in six). They have a decisive meeting with St. Louis on the final day, who are just ahead of them on goal difference but tied on points.

17. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 19

Sergi Roberto's first MLS goal was the icing on the cake of a 4-1 win against Austin that also featured Hirving Lozano's first goal back from injury and three assists from Marco Reus. Austin's not the toughest opponent in MLS this season, but the result matters as the Galaxy head into the final weekend still competing for a playoff spot.

18. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 20

The Crew may have lost the U.S. Open Cup final, but after beating D.C United 3-0, they're finishing the regular season on a five-game win streak. They confirmed their spot in the postseason and finished the weekend in one of the Eastern Conference's two wild card positions.

19. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 22

The Timbers secured a massive three points in a 3-1 win against the Dynamo highlighted by two assists and a goal from Vincent Janssen (nearly half his total goal contributions this year). With one game remaining, they're in a wild card spot and have one tentative hand on the playoffs.

20. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 23

In his first start since September, Joaquín Pereyra powered the Loons to three points with two goals against LAFC in a 3-1 win. They're still short of a final playoff spot (by two points) but following this result, they can still potentially break in with a win (and other results going in their favor), with San Jose waiting on the final day.

21. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 18

After falling behind 2-0 early to San Jose, Juan Manuel Sanabria's headed goal (his second of the year) in the 23rd minute provided life, but unfortunately nothing followed. They're currently outside the wild card spots ahead of a crucial final game against the Galaxy, but will also need some results to go their way.

22. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 12

RBNY had an early penalty stopped but came out with the upper hand against Nashville, taking a 2-0 lead in Tennessee that started with a beautiful link up between league wonderkids Adri Mehmeti and Julian Hall. But after two own goals and a stoppage-time winner from Nashville, the Red Bulls were eliminated from the playoffs in consecutive seasons for the first time ever.

23. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 21

After conceding a 91st-minute goal to last-placed Montréal, the Pigeons' playoff chances are officially over. A 1-1 draw isn't enough to launch them into the wild card position with one more game to go.

24. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 26

Dreyer -- a back-to-back MLS All-Star -- won't feature in this year's postseason, but that didn't stop him from handing the recently-crowded U.S. Open Cup champions a loss in a 1-0 victory over St. Louis. Dreyer's left-footed chip from distance was a taste of quality we'll be missing seven days from now.

25. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 24

With no postseason hopes, victories must come from small achievements, like letting Reus assist three goals or having a goalkeeper make six saves while still conceding four.

26. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 25

Toronto succumbed to a 3-1 defeat to Atlanta and ended their postseason dream in the process. Back to the drawing board for Robin Fraser's side, who showed signs of potential earlier in the season.

27. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 28

With the playoffs out of the picture and the all-time goals conceded in a single season record newly secured, SKC still did their best to sabotage Dallas by absconding with a 1-1 draw against a side looking to lock up their top-two finish in the Western Conference.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 29

Miguel Almirón won't appear in this year's playoffs, so he put on an end-of-season show in a 3-1 win against Toronto while eliminating the fellow Eastern Conference team from the playoffs. Five Stripes fans will take what they can get this year.

29. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 27

After losing to Toronto in the midweek, D.C. played Columbus with the playoffs already out of the picture and proceeded to lose 3-0. With 11 years since their last postseason victory, there's nowhere to go but up for this MLS original.

30. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

It's too late to save their season, but not too late to sink somebody else's. A 91st-minute response to NYCFC's 1-0 lead secured their 26th point of the year and put to rest New York's postseason dream.

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Manly shut down Paseka enquiry, Cowboys keen on Savage
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is heating up as we move beyond November 1. Isaac Issa has news on Bradman Best's future and which clubs might be lining up a play for Sam Walker.
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is heating up as we move beyond November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Manly shut down Paseka enquiry
Manly have knocked back an enquiry from Canberra about Taniela Paseka's availability, with the Sea Eagles unwilling to release the prop.

ESPN understands the Raiders initiated the enquiry, contrary to reports Paseka had been shopped to the club.

While Manly are looking to move on Luke Brooks and Ethan Bullemor as they reshape their roster, Paseka is a player they want to retain.

The front-rower remains contracted to the Sea Eagles until the end of 2029.

Ricky Stuart has since publicly denied Canberra are pursuing Paseka.

Cowboys among clubs eyeing Savage

North Queensland are among the clubs showing interest in Canberra winger Xavier Savage, as rivals assess their recruitment options for 2028.

ESPN understands the Cowboys and a Sydney-based club are keeping tabs on the speedster, who is contracted to the Raiders until the end of 2027 and became eligible to negotiate with rivals on November 1.

Savage scored 13 tries in 19 NRL appearances for Canberra this season.

Bryenton begins Tigers chapter

David Bryenton will begin full-time training with the Wests Tigers on Wednesday, with ESPN understanding the recruit features in Benji Marshall's long-term plans.

Having first reported his signing last month, ESPN can reveal Bryenton's mutually agreed release from the Bulldogs has now been finalised, clearing the way for him to join Marshall's squad for pre-season.

Dolphins win race for Su'a

The Dolphins have won the race to retain Sebastian Su'a, with ESPN understanding the young forward has agreed to terms on a two-year extension that will keep him in Redcliffe until the end of 2029.

Several NRL clubs had identified Su'a as a potential recruitment target, but the Dolphins have moved to secure his future with the club.

Fa'alogo agrees to long-term Storm extension

Sua Fa'alogo has agreed to extend his stay at the Melbourne Storm through to the end of 2032, ESPN understands.

The agreement will keep the fullback in Melbourne for the next six seasons, securing a key figure in the Storm's long-term plans.

Fa'alogo's retention delivers a major boost for Melbourne ahead of the November 1 contracting window, with the club moving to lock down one of its most exciting talents.

Dolphins close in on Lemuelu extension, confident of keeping Farnworth

The Dolphins are closing in on a multi-year extension for Connelly Lemuelu as they also express confidence in retaining Herbie Farnworth.

ESPN understands Lemuelu is nearing an agreement to extend his stay despite interest from Canberra, Parramatta and Cronulla.

Securing the back-rower would deliver a retention boost for the Dolphins, with the length of the proposed deal yet to be confirmed.

The club is also understood to be confident it can retain Farnworth despite links to the Sydney Roosters.

While that confidence is yet to translate into a confirmed extension, keeping the English international alongside Lemuelu would help preserve key combinations on the Dolphins' left edge.

Eels edge ahead in Best race
Parramatta have emerged as the frontrunners to land Bradman Best, with multiple sources indicating the Newcastle centre is increasingly likely to join the Eels beyond 2027.

Best has been identified as a priority target for Parramatta, who are looking to bolster Jason Ryles' backline with an established representative star.

While a deal is yet to be confirmed, the Eels are understood to be in the box seat despite Newcastle's efforts to retain him with a lucrative extension.

Bulldogs unlikely to enter Walker race
Canterbury are unlikely to enter the race for Sam Walker, with the Bulldogs backing their existing halfback options ahead of the upcoming season.

Despite suggestions the club could emerge as a potential destination for Walker, it is understood Canterbury are taking a wait-and-see approach rather than preparing to launch a pursuit.

The Bulldogs' immediate focus remains on the internal battle for the No.7 jersey, with Mitch and Alex Conti set to compete for the role over the offseason.

Canterbury have not completely shut the door on a move should circumstances change, but their current position suggests they are unlikely to become an active contender for Walker's signature.

For now, the Bulldogs are content to watch how the situation unfolds.
